messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Integration handshake + 5xx repro / next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Observations from your call: intermittent 5xx when your service calls /v1/generate (JSON tool-calling payloads, ~2–3% of requests during peak). SDK: Node 1.3.2, running behind an internal proxy.
- Hypothesis: transient auth handshake failures + routing mismatch (requests sometimes hitting a fallback variant) causing upstream 502/504 cascades.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) You send a representative trace/log excerpt (you mentioned a 5xx trace file) — we'll use it to correlate request IDs.
2) We'll provide a minimal repro script and a short Node snippet that toggles increased client timeout & keep-alive to rule out proxy timeouts.
3) Engineering triage: Marissa will own a short investigation and share recommended runtime flags or SDK patch if needed.

Attachments: sdk-sample.zip (example request), and a link to a short repro we plan to send.

If you can also paste the exact request headers (Authorization header format redacted is fine) and the timestamp of one failing request, that will let us look up server-side logs quickly.

Thanks — aiming to turn this into a targeted fix by tomorrow.

— Priyom
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration handshake + 5xx repro / next steps

Priyom — thanks for the summary. Attaching the trace we captured from our edge during the spike (trace-20260804.log). Key details:

- SDK: @redwood/sdk-node 1.3.2
- Failing endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Sample error snippet from our logs:
  [2026-08-04T16:45:12.927Z] requestId=sh_cY3k  status=502  message=UpstreamError: invalid handshake
  [2026-08-04T16:45:13.214Z] requestId=sh_cY3k  status=504  message=ReadTimeout

- We do see that the requests come from our proxy (internal IPs) and the Authorization header is present as a bearer token. We redacted the token and included the headers in the attached log.

Also: we tried bumping the client timeout to 30s as a quick test and saw the error rate drop, but not eliminated. We can reproduce the failure consistently if we send a steady stream of concurrent requests (about 200 rps) with a structured tool-calling payload — hits start after ~20 seconds.

Let us know what else you need. Happy to open a screen share if helpful.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration handshake + 5xx repro / next steps

Alex — Marissa here, engineering lead on SDK/runtime. Thanks for the trace — very helpful. Quick triage notes and a short repro plan: 

What I see from the trace:
- There are intermittent 502s with message "invalid handshake" coming from the LB -> runtime path, correlated with requestIds like sh_cY3k.
- Many of the failing requests show TCP FIN/RESET shortly before the 5xx, suggesting a downstream read timeout or connection reset.

Immediate checks for your side (quick, low-effort):
1) Confirm the Node SDK is not terminating sockets aggressively — set httpAgent keepAlive: true and maxSockets > concurrency. We have seen proxies that close idle sockets and cause handshake retries.
2) Add an explicit X-Redwood-Region header (us-west-2) to avoid routing to a fallback variant while we investigate routing rules.
3) Increase client timeout to 45s for the repro run (you already saw improvement at 30s).

I'll attach a tiny repro script (repro-script.sh) and a minimal Node snippet we recommend. If you can run the repro against a staging API key (or send a single failing requestId + timestamp), we'll pull server-side core dumps and the exact kernel call path.

Potential server-side mitigations we can push quickly (if you want us to):
- Relax the short-lived handshake window on the gateway for your account for 24 hours.
- Pin routing so your calls stay in the same model variant while we patch.

Related link: HubSpot deal (NW-2026-0114) — I'm flagging this for priority triage.

Next step: Priyom, can you confirm with Nimbus if they'll run the repro (Ben, can you join the screen when they do)?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Priyom — quick update from our end after running your repro: we implemented the keepAlive + X-Redwood-Region header and increased timeout to 45s. Results:

- Error rate dropped from ~2.6% to ~0.1% under the same 200 rps load test.
- We inspected the failing requestId you asked for (sh_cY3k) — the problem appears to be our proxy closing idle connections early during TLS handshake retries. We pushed a config change to keep sockets open slightly longer and the remaining failures disappeared.

Thanks for the rapid triage. We're comfortable moving forward with a short pilot (staging -> 2 services in prod) while we keep an eye on metrics. I'll start the DocuSign for the pilot order (link above) and loop procurement (Daniel).

If you want to formalize the short-term runtime flags (pin routing + handshake window relax), let me know and we'll approve.

— Alex
Alex Kline
Senior Platform Engineer, Nimbus Health
